messages.subject: R shiny matrix or table input
messages.subject_clean: R shiny matrix or table input
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to find a way to create a matrix or table as input for user to interact with in R shiny. For example, a matrix like this
sample name             number of tests
350292                  3
...                     ...

Ultimately, I want to automatically generate tabs in the mainPanel for user to input data for these different samples.

One way I find is through matrixInput in the package shinyIncubator, but this is an unofficial package and matrixInput function does not offer an option of column names. I tried the rhandsontable package, and used the following code.
library(shiny)
library(rhandsontable)

DF <- data.frame(name=c(350292, 360765), run=c(3,2))
colnames(DF) <- c("sample name", "number of tests")

ui <- fluidPage(
  headerPanel("test"),
  mainPanel(rHandsontableOutput("sample"))
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$sample <- renderRHandsontable({
    rhandsontable(DF, rowHeaders = NULL) %>%
     hot_col(c("sample name", "number of tests"), format = "0")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

But how to call values in the reactive rhandsontable? Eventually I want to be able to create tabs based on sample name and test number. In this case, it would be 350292_1, 350292_2, 350292_3, 360765_1, 360765_2.

messages.subject: Observers within ReactivePlots, re-evaluation issue
messages.subject_clean: Observers within ReactivePlots, re-evaluation issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
    I'm making an app where users can select data to create a "baseline" model. Then they can press the actionButton to duplicate the data.frame which stores the baseline within the final dataset, and then their new input from the "columns" input will be plotted alongside the "baseline" model they created (simply rbinding the baseline and new data.frame). Issues surround the Observers within ReactivePlots: 1) for some reason, the baseline is re-created each time the input option changes even though this is nested within the observeEvent which should not be re-evaluated without user input, and 2) the reset button creates an error within GGPLOT. Likely due to the same nesting issue.

Kind Regards and thanks in advance for any help you can provide on this issue,
       Conal Monaghan

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library("tidyr")
library("dplyr")
library("data.table")

# Lets make a fake dataset called "Data". Has 4 variable options and the Ages each data point relates to.
Ages <- 1:750
Variable1 <- rnorm(n=750, sd = 2, mean = 0)
Variable2 <- rnorm(n=750, sd = 1, mean = 2)
Variable3 <- rnorm(n=750, sd = 8, mean = 6)
Variable4 <- rnorm(n=750, sd = 3, mean = 3)

Data <- as.data.frame(cbind(Ages, Variable1, Variable2, Variable3, Variable4) )

### UI

ui <- fluidPage(
  checkboxGroupInput(inputId = "columns",
                     label = h4("Which Variables would you like in your  model?"),                    # Input Checkbox
                     choices =   c("Variable1", "Variable2", "Variable3", "Variable4")),

  plotOutput(outputId = "plot"),                                                        # Lets have our plot
  actionButton("base", "Create baseline"),                                  # Baseline action
  actionButton("reset", "Reset baseline")        # Reset Action
)  # Close UI

server <- function(input, output) {

  rVals <- reactiveValues() # Set up the reactive function outside the reactivePlot to prevent some issues with observers inside reactive functions

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    validate(need(!is.null(input$columns),  'Please tick a box to show a plot.'))   # Place a please choose columns for null input

    data <- gather(select(Data, "Ages", input$columns), variable, value, -Ages) ## Just doing a little data manipulation to change from wide to long form. This allows for calculations down the track and easier plotting

    # Now we can modify the data in some way, for example adding 1. Will     eventually add lots of model modifications here.

    data$value <- data$value + 1

    rVals[['data']] <- data              # Making a reactive values function. Place Data as "data".

    observeEvent(input$base,{
      baseline <- data
      baseline$variable <- paste("Baseline",
                                 baseline$variable, sep = "_")                    # Rename Variables to Baseline preamble
      rVals[['baseline']] <- baseline                                             # Put the new data into the reactive object under "baseline"
    })

    observeEvent(input$reset,{            # Reset button will wipe the data
      rVals[['baseline']] <- NULL
    })

    if(!is.null(rVals[['baseline']]))      # if a baseline has been created, then
    {rVals[['final']] <- bind_rows(rVals[['data']], rVals[['baseline']])           # Here we can simply bind the two datasets together if Baseline exists
    } else {rVals[['final']] <- rVals[['data']]}                                               # Otherwise we can use keep it as it is

    ## Make our Plot !

    ggplot(rVals[['final']], aes(x=Ages, y = as.numeric(value), colour = variable)) +    # variable = each dataset selected, value = respective values for that model
      labs(x="Age", y="value") +
      geom_line()

  })                              ## Close the render plot
}                                 ## Close the server
shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Re: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
messages.subject_clean: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
messages.body_plain:
Just letting you know that I also had to use this option to enable a fix for a Shiny app very recently, though it was only upon updating to R 3.4.1, not 3.4.0, where we started to get errors.

In specific, there was a section of the page where we would plot a highchart, and all would be fine. But upon changing one of the select boxes and trying to plot again, this is where we would get the seg fault and the app would crash. We tried a few things like updating all the packages so they were compiled in 3.4, making sure Cairo was installed, that "options(java.parameter...)" fix, etc. but the only thing that solved it was the "compiler::enableJIT(0)" line that the person above said

-Mike

On Thursday, June 1, 2017 at 6:34:29 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Wow, that's news to me! Do you have any idea what specific code in your Shiny app is triggering the segfault when jitting is on?
>
> On Thu, Jun 1, 2017 at 9:32 AM Jesse Bell <bellj...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > We had installed everything as root.  Good news is we seem to have found the solution.  It seems that the release of the Just In Time (JIT) compiler as part of 3.4.0 was the culprit.  This seems to be the specific problem related to shiny apps:
> >
> > https://www.r-statistics.com/2017/04/r-3-4-0-is-released-with-new-speed-upgrades-and-bug-fixes/
> > ("For now, the compiler will not compile code containing explicit calls to browser(): this is to support single stepping from the browser() call.")
> >
> > Adding the below line to the top of all of our app.R scripts has fixed (knock on wood) the problem.
> >
> > enableJIT(0)
> >
> > Thanks to our incredible Data Scientist, David Fackler for combing the release notes of 3.4.0 and putting together the pieces of the puzzle, and thanks to this group for all of the previous posts which helped us troubleshoot.  Hope this is helpful to others.

messages.body_plain:
Turns out its an R installation path issue. In root mode, when i type R in terminal, I can launch R but this is not the case in normal user mode. In normal user mode, I get exactly the same error found in log file, i.e., error while loading shared libraries: libicuuc.so.52: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory.
This means the path to R is not the same for both users (root and non-root user) and I have no idea why.

Troubleshooting and solution:
1. check that whether [which R@root] != [which R@normal_user], if true go to step #2
2. cp R in directory of R@root and overwrites the directory of R@normal_user with it (remember to backup first)

The reason for this hack is because those paths inside the script [which R@normal_user] are not the same as [which R@root]. I basically make the path [which R@normal_user] as a shortcut to [which R@root]. Any other solution is welcome. BTW, I have no idea why this happened. Probably I did some silly things because other languages like JAVA have congruent executable path among different users. One thing to note, the way I installed R on this centos6 machine is yum install R rather than build from source because my zlib on this machine is version 1.2.3 and version 1.2.5 is needed (even yum repo latest is 1.2.3) so it kinda failed on the configure step.

messages.body_plain:
Suppose I create a Shiny app as a function ie:

myApp <- function(param) {

randomNumber <- sample(1:10,1)

ui <- fluidPage(
        h1(param))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  x <- sample(1:10, 1)
  print(x * randomNumber)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

}

On Shiny Server I can create an app.R file with:

library(shiny)
myApp()

The scope of x is each session so it will be regenerated each view. In general variables defined outside of the server function are visible across sessions, but it is not clear if that is true in this case where the app is defined inside a function.

What is the scope of `randomNumber` in the above example? When I experiment with Shiny Server `randomNumber` appears to be regenerated each session, but I could be wrong.

Kind Regards,
Carl

messages.body_plain:
I am familiar with the idea of increasing the memory using something like the following in the server file:

options(shiny.maxRequestSize=300*1024^2) # 300 mg limit on file upload

However, I continue to wonder if this is the most optimal way to work in Shiny to accommodate variable data with different read in requirements.

For some background, I have an R program that parses fixed width files using functions from the sqldf package. Some of the fwf files are extremely large (possibly 10 million rows) and when using my function in base R the functions are extremely fast and yield the final output in minutes.

However, when running this same function in Shiny, even with increases in memory allocation, I get read in error (e.g., max upload size exceeded). Or, if I tinker with the line and increase the memory allocation some, I can get the files to load, but it takes an hour to load in Shiny but only minutes to load when using R.

Since I know that the version of R being used to run my Shiny app can easily read in and handle these data, is there a better way to allocate memory to the Shiny process instead of hard coding the max memory as in the sample line of code above?

That is, is there a way to allow for the Shiny app to have the same memory management properties as the version of R it is using to run on top of?

Thank you for any advice
Harold

formatDate(1:2, method = 'toLocaleTimeString',

messages.subject: Warning while using random values OR why I didn't get the same results in shiny and R console
messages.subject_clean: Warning while using random values OR why I didn't get the same results in shiny and R console
messages.body_plain:
I developed a code involving random values with control of the random seed in the R console, and couldn't get the same results within my Shiny app. It took me a while to find out that reactivity and lazy-evaluation led to the error. It seems obvious to me now. This post may help.

Here is a minimal example
The code could be

test <- function(a){
  set.seed(9380297)
  # Some code here involving a such as
  print(a)
  # more code
  return(paste(LETTERS[sample(x = 25,size=5,rep=TRUE)],collapse = ""))
}
a <- runif(1)
test(a)

leading to
[1] 0.3416042
[1] "HELLO"

In a Shiny app, using the same function test

library(shiny)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    actionButton("Button","Run"),
    verbatimTextOutput("out")
    ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    a <- reactive({input$Button
                  runif(1)})

    output$out <- renderPrint(test(a()))
  }
)

won't lead you to the same results. It's obvious since a is evaluated only when used, and "shift" the pseudo random values. It took me a while because "a" was used in the middle of a long function.

Solutions are to evaluate the parameters before setting the random seed (beginning of your function) or to set the random seed just before you use it...

test <- function(a){
  #If you are sure you'll need a, you can evaluate it at the beginning of the function  set.seed(9380297)
  a
  set.seed(9380297)
  # Some code here involving a such as
  print(a)
  # more code
  return(paste(LETTERS[sample(x = 25,size=5,rep=TRUE)],collapse = ""))
}

messages.subject_clean: Memory Limit
messages.body_plain:
Yes, Shiny's fileInput always uploads the complete file. If you want a different behavior, you'll have to modify it or create a custom file input.

Also, the "datapath" refers to the path of the file AFTER it's been uploaded. File inputs aren't allowed to get the actual path on a user's filesystem for security reasons. I think most browsers actually turn it into something like C:\fakepath\path-to-file
You can read files without uploading them to the server using HTML5's FileReader. But that would require custom HTML/JS to process the file.

So if your app is hosted on a remote system, you've got a tough challenge ahead. Even if you could get the actual file path on a user's system, the remote R server wouldn't be able to access it (without uploading).
You'll either have to upload the file or process it on the client side using an HTML5 FileReader.

If users can run the app on their local system, it's much easier. Just use the Shiny fileInput. The file "upload" would be copying the file to a temporary directory on the local system, which should be blazing fast.

So.. I'd still like to know where exactly the bottleneck is: the file upload itself or the processing after file upload? How long does it take to only upload a file to the server and do nothing else with it?

messages.subject: Saving plots for export using a counter
messages.subject_clean: Saving plots for export using a counter
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to incorporate an export feature into my app that allows users to save reactively updating plots as they make them via an action button and then download them in a batch later. The saved plots should go to a reactiveValues list, which will eventually be submitted to grid.arrange and exported as a .pdf. In the example below, I attempt to name plots for the list using a counter which will eventually be replaced by the system time. I create a string which contains the intended unique plot name, based on the counter. That works fine, and appears to add something to the list. However, when I attempt to investigate the object using browser(), it tells me that the saved plot is NULL. Is there an alternative way to rename a ggplot object or add it to a list? Or is there a more elegant way entirely to save plots for downloading in a batch?

# Intended sequence of events:
## 1. User makes plot
## 2. User clicks "save button,"
## 3. Plot goes to list of output objects, with name generated by counter

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

# Example UI

ui <- fluidPage(
  verticalLayout(
    titlePanel("Example"),
    plotOutput("plot1"),
    wellPanel(
      sliderInput("n", "Number of points", 10, 200,
                  value = 50, step = 10),

      actionButton("save", "Click here to save your graphics")   # save plot button

      # download plots button will go here.
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  count <- reactiveValues( i = 1)

  outputList <- reactiveValues(title = paste("Shiny outputs", Sys.Date()))   # make the list

  #make the plot

  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({

    outputList$plot1 <- ggplot()+
                        geom_point(aes(x = rnorm(input$n), y = rnorm(input$n)))+
                        theme_bw() # store the plot in the output list

    outputList$plot1 # print the plot for the ui
  })

  observe({input$save # When the user clicks the save button,

    isolate ({count$i <- count$i + 1}) # increase the counter by 1

    # paste("outputList$plot", count$i, sep = "") <- outputList$plot1 + ggtitle ("plot")
    ## tried pasting together the plot name. That didn't work b/c it thinks I'm trying to turn a plot into a string
    ## but I think this SHOULD work, and I don't understand why it doesn't:

    plotSlot <- paste("outputList$plot", count$i, sep = "") # make the output naming string

    assign(plotSlot, outputList$plot1)  # assign the name to the plot object
     #browser()
     })

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Re: renderDataTable - is it possible to sort by selected vs. unselected rows
messages.subject_clean: renderDataTable - is it possible to sort by selected vs. unselected rows
messages.body_plain:
DataTables supports dynamic table sorting with plugins. DT doesn't come with any, but you can add a plugin yourself, or take advantage of the Select extension.

The Select extension lets you add a checkbox column and sort it based on what's checked at the time. Rows selected in different pages are included.

Here's an example that demonstrates this:

https://gist.github.com/greg-lin/4a739b8375a4939498d5abd519fb6215

Note that it requires DT to use client-side processing in Shiny. If this is an issue, you could sort the table on the server-side using input$NAME_rows_selected

It's also possible to do this without the Select extension (sort with a button click or something), but I think a checkbox column is intuitive enough for users.

messages.subject_clean: renderDataTable - is it possible to sort by selected vs. unselected rows
messages.body_plain:
Client-side processing means the entire table is sent to your browser at once, and further sorted/paged/searched by your browser. It's not efficient with large data sets (like thousands, millions of rows).
Server-side processing means the server does all the processing, and only sends one page of data to your browser at a time. This is what DT uses by default in Shiny, but you can disable it by setting server = FALSE in DT::renderDataTable

http://rstudio.github.io/DT/server.html
https://datatables.net/manual/server-side

The custom data sorting plugins operate completely in the browser. They wouldn't do anything if the server controlled the data sorting.

i select the records that has no value in the gender column of my dataset, how to
write this condition in server.R?

Issue 2) "Standard Category" is another input from user where I've used radioButtons
that has options "All" and "Multiple Select", if "Multiple Select" is selected,
I've used selectInput with which user can select multiple options,

**Warning: Error in match: object 'broad_cat' not found"**, or **Error : object
'broad_cat' not found**, this I am not sure if persists because of any error in my
previous code, because this is correct syntactically.

g <- reactive(subset(o(), broad_cat %in% input$broad_cat))

messages.body_plain:
shiny server open source does not support multiple users at the same time (per app), which means that when one user's session runs a query or some calculation, other users will not be able to perform any actions in the app.
you can solve it by either providing your users with local versions of the shiny app (to run using rstudio/docker), or by duplicating the app on the server - one copy per team/user. the open-source shiny server supports multiple apps (processes) running at the same time.

messages.subject: Re: Observers within ReactivePlots, re-evaluation issue
messages.subject_clean: Observers within ReactivePlots, re-evaluation issue
messages.body_plain:
It's almost never correct to create new observers, reactives, etc. inside of a renderPlot or any other render function. It's less rare, but still pretty uncommon, to create new observers, reactives, etc. inside of observers (usually relate to creating new UI).

You do want to hoist all of your observers and reactive expressions up to the server function scope, and convert all the observers you can into reactive expressions. In this case, the only bit that can't be made into a reactive expression is the baseline, because you can reset it with a button (therefore it's not a "pure" stateless calculation--the baseline has to encode the memory of whether you clicked input$base or input$reset last, and that means needing a reactive value(s)).

Here's what I came up with:

ui <- fluidPage(
  checkboxGroupInput(inputId = "columns",
    label = h4("Which Variables would you like in your  model?"),                    # Input Checkbox
    choices =   c("Variable1", "Variable2", "Variable3", "Variable4")),

  plotOutput(outputId = "plot"),                                                        # Lets have our plot
  actionButton("base", "Create baseline"),                                  # Baseline action
  actionButton("reset", "Reset baseline")        # Reset Action
)  # Close UI

server <- function(input, output) {

  # Making a reactive as "data".
  data <- reactive({

    validate(need(!is.null(input$columns),  'Please tick a box to show a plot.'))   # Place a please choose columns for null input

    data <- gather(select(Data, "Ages", input$columns), variable, value, -Ages) ## Just doing a little data manipulation to change from wide to long form. This allows for calculations down the track and easier plotting

    # Now we can modify the data in some way, for example adding 1. Will     eventually add lots of model modifications here.

    data$value <- data$value + 1

    data
  })

  r_baseline <- reactiveVal(NULL)

  observeEvent(input$base,{
    baseline <- data()

    baseline$variable <- paste("Baseline",
      baseline$variable, sep = "_")            # Rename Variables to Baseline preamble

    r_baseline(baseline)                       # Put the new data into the reactive object under "r_baseline"
  })

  observeEvent(input$reset, {
    r_baseline(NULL)
  })

  final <- reactive({
    if(!is.null(r_baseline())) {               # if a baseline has been created, then
      bind_rows(data(), r_baseline())          # Here we can simply bind the two datasets together if Baseline exists
    } else {
      data() # Otherwise we can use keep it as it is
    }
  })

  output$plot <- renderPlot({

    ## Make our Plot !

    ggplot(final(), aes(x=Ages, y = as.numeric(value), colour = variable)) +    # variable = each dataset selected, value = respective values for that model

      labs(x="Age", y="value") +
      geom_line()
  })                              ## Close the render plot
}                                 ## Close the server
shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Re: Multi Step Analysis in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Multi Step Analysis in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Generally people do this with multiple tabs. You can also do this with a renderUI if you don't want to let people jump backward and forward between different steps; create a separate Shiny module for each step, and create a reactiveVal() to track which step the user is currently on, and use a uiOutput/renderUI in your main UI which will display the UI of whichever module corresponds to the current step.

messages.subject: Re: iterative simulation in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: iterative simulation in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Is there a reason you want each week to be a separate reactive? How about a single eventReactive() that creates and populates week.remain using a for-loop and returns it? The only reason not to do this is if the different weeks had different "lifetimes" (i.e. you'd want to update weeks 4 and later without having to re-run weeks 1-3) but that seems not to be the case here.

(And if you did want to do that, then you'd make a list of reactives [rather than what I'm suggesting above, which is a reactive that returns a list], not separate variables, I'd think.)

messages.subject_clean: can shiny be used to build a dynamic webpage
messages.body_plain:
What Shiny Server Open Source doesn't support is multiple *R processes* per app, but each R process can support multiple simultaneous users. It does mean that calculations cannot be performed concurrently though, so all the requests are serialized. For 50 concurrent users, it really depends on how latent your database is and how often each user is reading/writing. In the future you will also be able to use Shiny's upcoming async functionality (though this will be rightfully considered pretty advanced).

Then they can press the actionButton to duplicate the data.frame which stores the baseline within the final dataset, and then their new input from the "columns" input will be plotted alongside the "baseline" model they created (simply rbinding the baseline and new data.frame). Issues surround the Observers within ReactivePlots: 1) for some reason, the baseline is re-created each time the input option changes even though this is nested within the observeEvent which should not be re-evaluated without user input, and 2) the reset button creates an error within GGPLOT. Likely due to the same nesting issue.
>
> Kind Regards and thanks in advance for any help you can provide on this issue,
>        Conal Monaghan
>
>
>
>
>
> library(shiny)
> library(ggplot2)
> library("tidyr")
> library("dplyr")
> library("data.table")
>
> # Lets make a fake dataset called "Data". Has 4 variable options and the Ages each data point relates to.
> Ages <- 1:750
> Variable1 <- rnorm(n=750, sd = 2, mean = 0)
> Variable2 <- rnorm(n=750, sd = 1, mean = 2)
> Variable3 <- rnorm(n=750, sd = 8, mean = 6)
> Variable4 <- rnorm(n=750, sd = 3, mean = 3)
>
> Data <- as.data.frame(cbind(Ages, Variable1, Variable2, Variable3, Variable4) )
>
>
>
> ### UI
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   checkboxGroupInput(inputId = "columns",
>                      label = h4("Which Variables would you like in your  model?"),                    # Input Checkbox
>                      choices =   c("Variable1", "Variable2", "Variable3", "Variable4")),
>
>   plotOutput(outputId = "plot"),                                                        # Lets have our plot
>   actionButton("base", "Create baseline"),                                  # Baseline action
>   actionButton("reset", "Reset baseline")        # Reset Action
> )  # Close UI
>
> server <- function(input, output) {
>
>   rVals <- reactiveValues() # Set up the reactive function outside the reactivePlot to prevent some issues with observers inside reactive functions
>
>   output$plot <- renderPlot({
>     validate(need(!is.null(input$columns),  'Please tick a box to show a plot.'))   # Place a please choose columns for null input
>
>     data <- gather(select(Data, "Ages", input$columns), variable, value, -Ages) ## Just doing a little data manipulation to change from wide to long form. This allows for calculations down the track and easier plotting
>
>     # Now we can modify the data in some way, for example adding 1. Will     eventually add lots of model modifications here.
>
>     data$value <- data$value + 1
>
>     rVals[['data']] <- data              # Making a reactive values function. Place Data as "data".
>
>     observeEvent(input$base,{
>       baseline <- data
>       baseline$variable <- paste("Baseline",
>                                  baseline$variable, sep = "_")                    # Rename Variables to Baseline preamble
>       rVals[['baseline']] <- baseline                                             # Put the new data into the reactive object under "baseline"
>     })
>
>     observeEvent(input$reset,{            # Reset button will wipe the data
>       rVals[['baseline']] <- NULL
>     })
>
>     if(!is.null(rVals[['baseline']]))      # if a baseline has been created, then
>     {rVals[['final']] <- bind_rows(rVals[['data']], rVals[['baseline']])           # Here we can simply bind the two datasets together if Baseline exists
>     } else {rVals[['final']] <- rVals[['data']]}                                               # Otherwise we can use keep it as it is
>
>     ## Make our Plot !
>
>     ggplot(rVals[['final']], aes(x=Ages, y = as.numeric(value), colour = variable)) +    # variable = each dataset selected, value = respective values for that model
>       labs(x="Age", y="value") +
>       geom_line()
>
>   })                              ## Close the render plot
> }                                 ## Close the server
> shinyApp(ui, server)

Hi Jerry,
Are you confident that digest was installed properly?

I ask because I know at least Centos 6.3 doesn't ship (by default) with a gcc new enough to compile parts of Shiny's dependencies. I remember seeing a similar error on Centos and it ended up being related to problems compiling C++. I just know that for the Shiny Server build we go through special hoops to use "scl" to make a newer gcc available [1][2].

I'm pretty sure Centos 7 has a suitable gcc by default, so if you can I recommend using that instead. Install procedure is identical.

Alan

On Thursday, April 6, 2017 at 10:47:39 AM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> True! And in fact, the interval-based checking is itself done in an observer, so I believe that if your file-path-returning function does access reactive inputs/values/expressions, the checking will happen as soon as those reactives change, not waiting for the interval to elapse.
>
> On Wed, Apr 5, 2017 at 4:32 PM Peter Andrews <pand...@alumni.brown.edu> wrote:
> > I know this is very old but for those interested... the myfile does not need to a reactive but simply a function that returns the current filePath. Because the reactiveFileReader runs at an interval it will call the function every time so there is no need for myfile to be a reactive. Key idea is that rather than passing a value you pass a function to get that value. That level of indirectness makes it work.
> >
> >
> > On Saturday, November 7, 2015 at 3:25:09 PM UTC-5, Ted Mendum wrote:
> > > Hi All,
> > >
> > > I would like to read (and periodically poll) a log file that the user has selected through the gui (using, e.g., choose.files()).  Unfortunately, the filePath argument to reactiveFileReader does not allow the use of reactives.  So something like
> > >
> > > file_contents <- reactiveFileReader(1000, session, filePath = myfile(), readFunc = scan, what = "character", sep = "\n")
> > >
> > > where myfile() is some reactive that returns the file name as a  string will fail with the message:
> > >
> > > Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() :
> > >   Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)
> > >
> > > How can I get a value for the filePath which is chosen by the user but is not a reactive?
> > >
> > > Some constraints on acceptable solutions:
> > > 1) The name of the log file will change every time the app is used.
> > > 2) The user can't type the log file name in using textInput or the like because I am generating the file dynamically, nor do I want to deal with potential typos.
> > >
> > > A reproducible example is below.
> > >
> > > library(shiny)
> > >
> > > ui <- fluidPage(
> > >     headerPanel("Reactive File Reader"),
> > >     sidebarPanel(
> > >         actionButton("pick_file", "Pick File"),
> > >         verbatimTextOutput("pick_file")
> > >     ),
> > >     mainPanel(
> > >         textOutput("file_contents")
> > >     )
> > > )
> > >
> > > server <- function(input, output, session){
> > >     file_name <- eventReactive(
> > >         input$pick_file,
> > >         file.choose()
> > >     )
> > >
> > >
> > >     output$pick_file <- renderText(
> > >         file_name()
> > >     )
> > >
> > >
> > >     file_contents <- reactiveFileReader(1000, session, filePath = file_name(),
> > >                                          readFunc = scan, what = "character",sep = "\n")
> > >
> > >     output$file_contents <- renderText(file_contents())
> > >
> > > }
> > >
> > > shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
> > >
> > > Thanks,
> > >
> > > Ted

messages.body_plain:
take a look at the accordion sidebar from the package bsplus <http://ijlyttle.github.io/bsplus/articles/accordion_sidebar.html>.
make sure to pipe the bs options for desired behavior, for example - the following line of code will case the entire title bar to be clickable, not just the text
# code for creating an accordion sidebar in your ui file/section
bs_accordion("id")%>%

# code for making the entire title clickable
bs_set_opts(use_heading_link = TRUE) %>%

# accordion sidebar with checkbox groups
bs_append(title = "title", content = checkboxGroupInput(...))

messages.body_plain:
Your code is overly complicated. This is enough:

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("action", "action"),
  tableOutput("txt_example1")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  x <- reactiveVal(matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4), nrow = 2))
  observeEvent(input$action, { x(x() + 1) })
  output$txt_example1 <- renderTable({ x() })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

And yes, this method is scalable to other complex R objects.

Hi Chien,

Indeed, you raise a good point, I only tested it under Linux and there it works slightly differently as the forking creates an identical copy of the process and thus the reactive context is avaialable.

I have fixed the gist to work properly under Windows as well, the only change was that I now wrap automatically the handler expression with `isolate` so that Shiny doesn't throw an error under the new process.

Let me know if now it works for you,

Best,

Andras

> > > > > > > However this approach also has a few small drawbacks: 1) it's not possible to have side-effects in the handler expression, 2) The reactive produced by my async version will not invalidate downstream when the calculation starts, but instead when the calculation finishes and the value is returned. This means that the 'recalculating' class (opacity) is not applied to an output depending on the async reactive whilst the calculation is running.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > The reason why I thought to make eventReactive async is that the event expression (usually the fast part) can remain synchronous and the long-running handler expression can be sent for async evaluation. Also, by creating an async version of a 'reactive' it's relatively a minor issue that side-effects are not allowed for in the handler expression.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > I would be very curious to know what others have been doing to have async / non-blocking behaviour in Shiny. Also, as far as I know there is an 'async' version of Shiny being worked on, I would be interested if there is some information on what the underlying approach taken is.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Cheers,
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Andras
